{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "ryanofsky",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept and approach ACK; provided rebase branches, suggested separating move-only commits and removing indirection overhead"
    },
    {
      "login": "ajtowns",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Raised concerns regarding std::function overhead, global initialization order regressions, and conditional evaluation of LogInfo arguments"
    },
    {
      "login": "purpleKarrot",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Objected to singleton pattern usage in the logger and questioned the multi-connection logging interface"
    },
    {
      "login": "w0xlt",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Found potential resource leaks and a mutex deadlock risk if bad_alloc occurs during callback registration"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "rc:2720705368",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "LogInfo called during global initialization prior to InitLogger() could fail or misbehave with a shared dispatcher",
      "quote": "This seems like a regression. With this approach you can't assume LogInfo called during global initialization won't be called prior to InitLogger()",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2721990582",
        "rc:2729164905",
        "c:3801642121"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:2729164905",
      "settled_by_quote": "I've changed the approach to your suggestion, so marking this as resolved."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2720709919",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "Unnecessary performance overhead in log-checking paths caused by std::function indirection",
      "quote": "Jumping through a std::function when we could just be checking an atomic bitfield doesn't seem like a good approach.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2721327278",
        "rc:2736442108",
        "rc:3981133644"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3981133644",
      "settled_by_quote": "The indirection is gone, and this PR now doesn't touch util/node logging (including logging statement evaluation) at all"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2734793117",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "Breaks code that relies on side-effects inside logging arguments if LogInfo argument evaluation is made conditional",
      "quote": "I think your latest implementation (a4e8f3c8d6763a95c1804fc40781b379e6127b66) is dangerously wrong, btw -- LogInfo() etc currently always evaluate their arguments",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2736442108",
        "rc:2737382315",
        "c:3812232408"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:2749146860",
      "settled_by_quote": "The easiest way to ensure any potential/accidental side-effects don't make the behaviour brittle is to always evaluate the logging statements, which is what our code currently does"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:3803203999",
      "kind": "interface",
      "harm": "Unnecessary complexity from supporting multi-connection callbacks and userdata when the logger is internally global",
      "quote": "I doubt that there is an actual use case for multiple logging connections. The logger is global internally and can be handled as global by clients as well",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:3804631039"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "c:3804631039",
      "settled_by_quote": "I think this concern is orthogonal to the changes proposed in this PR, so I think that conversation might be better had e.g. in #30342 ?"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2730355874",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "Using singletons introduces viral coupling across kernel components",
      "quote": "Now everybody should understand why singletons are *viral* and therefore should be forbidden. I have zero tolerance for such code.",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "open",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2731541954"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "",
      "settled_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3984322784",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "Memory leak of user_data and connection allocation if std::bad_alloc is thrown during callback registration",
      "quote": "RegisterCallback() and LogDebug() can also throw std::bad_alloc. btck_LoggingConnection can be a smart pointer.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3988186475",
        "rc:4006655804",
        "c:5679317242"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:4006655804",
      "settled_by_quote": "Fixed by wrapping user data in a RAII UserData wrapper, and the callback in a RAII CallbackHandle wrapper."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4030551866",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "Deadlock if std::bad_alloc during list insertion destroys temporary callback while holding the logger mutex and user_data destruction interacts with the logger",
      "quote": "If that callback destroys another logging connection, it tries to acquire the same mutex and deadlocks, preventing btck_logging_connection_create from returning nullptr.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4034240501",
        "c:5712024212"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "c:5712024212",
      "settled_by_quote": "Force-pushed to address a (hard to reach) deadlock issue flagged by @w0xlt"
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:3813719678",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "Major concept and approach ACK. This seems thoughtfully implemented to be minimally disruptive to existing code while rationalizing the kernel logging API",
      "substantive": true
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Objections from ajtowns (std::function overhead, side effects, init ordering) and w0xlt (bad_alloc leaks and callback mutex deadlock) were resolved with pushed fixes. purpleKarrot's objection against singletons remains open as the author asked for alternatives without follow-up."
}

participants.note: Concept and approach ACK; provided rebase branches, suggested separating move-only commits and removing indirection overhead
Raised concerns regarding std::function overhead, global initialization order regressions, and conditional evaluation of LogInfo arguments
Objected to singleton pattern usage in the logger and questioned the multi-connection logging interface
Found potential resource leaks and a mutex deadlock risk if bad_alloc occurs during callback registration

claims.harm: LogInfo called during global initialization prior to InitLogger() could fail or misbehave with a shared dispatcher
claims.quote: This seems like a regression. With this approach you can't assume LogInfo called during global initialization won't be called prior to InitLogger()

claims.harm: Unnecessary performance overhead in log-checking paths caused by std::function indirection
claims.quote: Jumping through a std::function when we could just be checking an atomic bitfield doesn't seem like a good approach.
claims.settled_by_quote: The indirection is gone, and this PR now doesn't touch util/node logging (including logging statement evaluation) at all

claims.harm: Breaks code that relies on side-effects inside logging arguments if LogInfo argument evaluation is made conditional
claims.quote: I think your latest implementation (a4e8f3c8d6763a95c1804fc40781b379e6127b66) is dangerously wrong, btw -- LogInfo() etc currently always evaluate their arguments
claims.settled_by_quote: The easiest way to ensure any potential/accidental side-effects don't make the behaviour brittle is to always evaluate the logging statements, which is what our code currently does

claims.harm: Unnecessary complexity from supporting multi-connection callbacks and userdata when the logger is internally global
claims.quote: I doubt that there is an actual use case for multiple logging connections. The logger is global internally and can be handled as global by clients as well
claims.settled_by_quote: I think this concern is orthogonal to the changes proposed in this PR, so I think that conversation might be better had e.g. in #30342 ?

claims.harm: Using singletons introduces viral coupling across kernel components
claims.quote: Now everybody should understand why singletons are *viral* and therefore should be forbidden. I have zero tolerance for such code.

claims.harm: Memory leak of user_data and connection allocation if std::bad_alloc is thrown during callback registration
claims.quote: RegisterCallback() and LogDebug() can also throw std::bad_alloc. btck_LoggingConnection can be a smart pointer.
claims.settled_by_quote: Fixed by wrapping user data in a RAII UserData wrapper, and the callback in a RAII CallbackHandle wrapper.

claims.harm: Deadlock if std::bad_alloc during list insertion destroys temporary callback while holding the logger mutex and user_data destruction interacts with the logger
claims.quote: If that callback destroys another logging connection, it tries to acquire the same mutex and deadlocks, preventing btck_logging_connection_create from returning nullptr.
claims.settled_by_quote: Force-pushed to address a (hard to reach) deadlock issue flagged by @w0xlt

support.reason: Major concept and approach ACK. This seems thoughtfully implemented to be minimally disruptive to existing code while rationalizing the kernel logging API

result.notes: Objections from ajtowns (std::function overhead, side effects, init ordering) and w0xlt (bad_alloc leaks and callback mutex deadlock) were resolved with pushed fixes. purpleKarrot's objection against singletons remains open as the author asked for alternatives without follow-up.
